newsitem.title: UK: UK shares advances as bid talk spreads.
newsitem.headline: UK shares advances as bid talk spreads.

text.p: UK shares tracked futures higher late Monday morning, with sentiment underpinned by bid hopes despite a renewed surge in sterling.
The FTSE 100 index was up 23.5 points to 4,823.0 by 1022 GMT. Advancing stocks outpaced decliners by five-to-four.
"Everyone is talking about mergers," said one dealer. "Sterling worries and rate rises have been pushed into the background."
Pharmaceutical stocks led the way, with Zeneca, SmithKline Beecham and Glaxo Wellcome contributing 12 points of the FTSE rise.
The sector was buoyed by hopes of corporate activity and a positive note from broker NatWest Securities.
News that chemicals giant ICI had agreed to sell its polyester polymer, titanium dioxide and polyester film businesses to U.S. firm DuPont Co for $3 billion also helped to lift the mood.
Banks and retail stocks gathered strength and were not put off by sterling's rise to 6-1/2 year highs.
"The consumer sector will continue to lead the market despite the strength of sterling," said another dealer. "Especially with hints of merger activity in the background."
UK gilts, meanwhile, fell back to be lower on the day despite weaker-than-expected producer price data which showed the lack of price pressures at the producer level.
"The PPI numbers were fairly healthy but they were pretty much ignored," one trader said.
"The data just confirmed that the manufacturing sector remains weak," added Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon.
Trading activity remained relatively subdued with dealers noting "big moves on small volumes" as the outlook was further interest rate rises and sterling left some investors uneasy.

The latest Merrill Lynch/Gallup survey found that UK fund managers were shifting from equities into UK gilts in response to higher base rates, the strong pound and the abolition of dividend tax credits for pension funds.
The survey, taken after the British budget, found the biggest number of net buyers of UK gilts since 1994.

"What we are seeing is a switch of domestic assets. UK equities look expensive against gilts," said Merrill Lynch strategist Bijal Shah. "Fund managers do not believe sterling is going to weaken significantly in the next twelve months, so they do not want to be out of sterling assets."
Among individual share movers ICI leapt 63p to 873-1/2p. Glaxo Wellcome was up 26-1/2p to 13.43-1/2 stg, SmithKline Beecham was up 28p to 12.32 stg and Zeneca was up 51-1/2p to 21.31-1/2 stg.
Shares in WH Smith climbed 10p to 351-1/2p after a weekend press report said the UK retailer was thought to be the target of a bid.
Commercial Union gained 17p to 696-1/2p on speculation that ABN Amro Holding NV may be interested in buying the company.
